reference: GNU coreutils rmdir(1) from the runner's reference PATH, with GNU mkdir and ln used only to create private fixtures. Each parity script runs unchanged under system Bash and bash-os with candidate PATH empty; failures are captured where effects must still be inspected. The metadata contract uses the stock Bash rmdir documentation and builtin type metadata.
coverage: Remove one empty directory and verify the tree is empty.
Remove nested directories with separate child-then-parent operands.
GNU -p parent removal, including partial removal and final error status.
Handle a spaced path and a dash-prefixed basename through a ./ path.
Accept a trailing slash on an empty directory operand.
Reject a nonempty directory and preserve its contents.
Report a missing operand path and retain the expected filesystem state.
Continue across operands after a nonempty-directory error and remove a later empty directory.
Reject a symlink to a directory without removing either link or target.
Compare the no-operand error status and verify builtin/help registration.
Additional bounded edge cases and file effects are specified by the added parity cases.
GNU --ignore-fail-on-non-empty with -p, continued operands, real errors and the option terminator.
Guest pass 5 (G74/G78): GNU long options, abbreviations and diagnostics, and the -c/-v/-d/-I/--reference behaviours of coreutils 9.7.
Clean-room rewrite (MIT): -p ancestor diagnostics, symlink operands with trailing slashes and --ignore-fail-on-non-empty over permission errors.
exclusions: Permission-denied and read-only-filesystem cases are omitted because this fixture does not set up independent privilege or mount conditions.
Exact diagnostic wording is not asserted; stderr presence or absence and resulting tree are checked.
No host, device, network, privileged, stress, or destructive system operations are involved.
GNU --ignore-fail-on-non-empty is explicitly compared; --verbose and long-option combinations are not exhaustive.

cases.purpose: Remove one empty relative directory and verify successful status, no output, and removal.
cases.script: mkdir target; rmdir target; [[ ! -e target ]]; printf 'removed\n'

cases.purpose: Remove an empty child and then its parent as two ordered operands.
cases.script: mkdir top; mkdir top/inner; rmdir top/inner top; [[ ! -e top ]]; printf 'removed\n'

cases.purpose: Check GNU rmdir -p semantics, capturing command status so the parent-removal effect is compared even if the candidate rejects the option.
cases.script: mkdir chain; mkdir chain/leaf; set +e; rmdir -p chain/leaf; rc=$?; set -e; if [[ -e chain ]]; then parent=retained; else parent=removed; fi; printf 'status=%s parent=%s\n' "$rc" "$parent"

cases.purpose: Remove a path containing spaces and a dash-prefixed directory addressed through ./.
cases.script: mkdir 'two words'; mkdir ./-odd; rmdir 'two words' ./-odd; [[ ! -e 'two words' && ! -e ./-odd ]]; printf 'removed 2\n'

cases.purpose: Accept a trailing slash on an empty directory operand.
cases.script: mkdir trailing; rmdir trailing/; [[ ! -e trailing ]]; printf 'removed\n'

cases.purpose: Return failure for a nonempty directory while preserving the directory and its file.
cases.script: mkdir nonempty; printf 'payload\n' > nonempty/file; set +e; rmdir nonempty; rc=$?; set -e; if [[ -e nonempty/file ]]; then state=retained; else state=missing; fi; printf 'status=%s file=%s\n' "$rc" "$state"

cases.purpose: Report a nonexistent directory operand, capture its status, and leave the fixture tree unchanged.
cases.script: set +e; rmdir missing; rc=$?; set -e; printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Verify that a nonempty first operand does not prevent removal of a later empty operand; also include a missing operand in the aggregate failure.
cases.script: mkdir blocked; printf 'keep\n' > blocked/file; mkdir later; set +e; rmdir blocked later absent; rc=$?; set -e; if [[ -e blocked/file ]]; then blocked_state=retained; else blocked_state=missing; fi; if [[ -e later ]]; then later_state=retained; else later_state=removed; fi; printf 'status=%s blocked=%s later=%s\n' "$rc" "$blocked_state" "$later_state"

cases.purpose: Reject a symlink operand and leave both the symlink and its empty target directory intact.
cases.script: mkdir target; ln -s target link; set +e; rmdir link; rc=$?; set -e; if [[ -L link && -d target ]]; then state=retained; else state=changed; fi; printf 'status=%s state=%s\n' "$rc" "$state"

cases.purpose: Compare the utility-level failure status for a no-operand invocation while capturing it to keep the fixture script successful.
cases.script: set +e; rmdir; rc=$?; set -e; printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Assert Bash reports rmdir as a builtin and that its documented help entry exists, without treating metadata as operation coverage.
cases.script: type -t rmdir; help rmdir >metadata.discard

cases.purpose: The -- terminator allows a dash-leading directory.
cases.script: mkdir ./-target; rmdir -- -target

cases.purpose: Parent removal handles repeated and trailing separators.
cases.script: mkdir -p chain/a/b; rmdir -p chain//a//b///

cases.purpose: Parent removal stops with failure at a nonempty ancestor, retaining its other contents.
cases.script: mkdir -p tree/a/b; printf keep > tree/retained; rmdir -p tree/a/b

cases.purpose: An explicit dot ancestor is attempted and diagnosed after its empty children are removed.
cases.script: mkdir -p tree/leaf; rmdir -p ./tree/leaf

cases.purpose: Parent removal stops at a nonempty ancestor after removing its empty child; later operands are processed.
cases.script:
mkdir -p top/child later
printf keep > top/file
rc=0; rmdir -p top/child later || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: GNU ignore-nonempty option suppresses only the nonempty-directory error and preserves the directory contents.
cases.script:
mkdir box
printf keep > box/file
rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty box

cases.purpose: Combine -p and the ignore option before operands: remove the empty leaf, ignore a nonempty ancestor, and process a later empty directory.
cases.script:
mkdir -p parent/leaf empty
printf keep > parent/keep
rmdir -p --ignore-fail-on-non-empty parent/leaf empty

cases.purpose: Missing and regular-file operands still fail under ignore-nonempty, while later empty directories are removed.
cases.script:
mkdir box empty
printf keep > box/file
printf regular > plain
rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty box absent plain empty

cases.purpose: The terminator permits a directory whose name is the ignore option without enabling the option.
cases.script:
mkdir -- --ignore-fail-on-non-empty
rmdir -- --ignore-fail-on-non-empty

cases.purpose: rmdir --parents, --verbose, abbreviations, --ignore-fail-on-non-empty and GNU's verbose and failure lines (G74).
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
mkdir -p x/y/z a/b q/r; : > q/r/f
n rmdir --parents --verbose x/y/z
n rmdir --pa -v a/b
n rmdir --verbose q/r | s
n rmdir --ign q/r
n rmdir -p --ignore q/r
n rmdir --bogus q | s
ls

cases.purpose: rmdir -pv stops at the first ancestor that cannot be removed and reports it.
rmdir -p reports a failing ancestor as 'failed to remove directory', except a symlink ancestor (Not a directory), and stops at '.' and '..' prefixes.
A symlink operand: 'Not a directory' without a trailing slash, 'Symbolic link not followed' with one (also when dangling); a file with a slash stays 'Not a directory'.
--ignore-fail-on-non-empty also hides a refusal (Permission denied, Device or resource busy) of a directory that is not empty, but not of an empty one, nor '.' (Invalid argument).
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //g'; }
if [[ $EUID == 0 ]]; then echo 'skipped: running as root'; exit 0; fi
mkdir -p r/full r/empty; : > r/full/f; chmod 555 r
n rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty r/full | s; n rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty -pv r/full | s; n rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty r/empty | s; n rmdir r/full | s
n rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty . | s; n rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty .. | s
chmod 755 r; ls -R r
